subject: Internal beta: feedback summary + decisions for public launch readiness (Quickstart Templates)
body:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Mar 10, 2025 at 9:12 AM
Subject: Internal beta: feedback summary + decisions for public launch readiness (Quickstart Templates)

Team — here’s the roll-up from internal beta (last 10 days) + the proposed fix/defer list for public launch.

Overall signal
- Template value is clear ("I got a working RAG app with traces in < 20 mins"), but we’re still tripping folks on first-run friction + a couple defaults that look too aggressive for self-serve quotas.
- Biggest risk to public launch is support load from the same 4 issues repeating.

Top issues (by frequency / severity)
P0 (must address before public launch)
1) Telemetry tag header blocked by corporate proxies / strict gateways
   - Symptoms: 4xx from customer proxy, or requests never reaching us
   - Threads/tickets: SUP-29458, incident-adjacent notes from internal testers
   - Proposal: make template-origin telemetry opt-in + default OFF; document how to enable

2) 429s / rate limiting hit quickly with current concurrency defaults
   - Symptoms: users hit 429 on first load test; retry storms in worst cases
   - Tickets: SUP-29435 + internal #help reports
   - Proposal: lower default concurrency + add backoff guidance + “starter tier safe” preset

3) Local OTel collector / exporter misconfig causes “no traces” confusion
   - Symptoms: app runs but no spans in Console; OTLP auth/endpoint issues
   - Tickets: SUP-29422 + internal thread
   - Proposal: stronger doctor checks + docs troubleshooting + clearer env var naming

4) Streaming disconnects behind certain proxies / load balancers
   - Symptoms: broken streams, partial responses; retries sometimes double-charge tokens in perception
   - Tickets: SUP-29410
   - Proposal: document recommended proxy settings + implement safer reconnect behavior in SDK/template

P1 (strongly preferred for launch, but can ship if we have mitigations + docs)
5) macOS install friction for python deps (build tools, SSL, etc.)
   - Symptoms: pip install fails; unclear next step
   - Internal: #help thread

6) Agent tool schema parse errors are confusing; error message doesn’t tell you what to fix
   - Tickets: SUP-29441

P2 (defer unless low-effort)
7) Additional vector store adapters beyond local default
8) Additional deployment recipes beyond Docker + one hosted example
9) “Upgrade story” for template versions beyond “re-init latest” guidance

Decisions I’m proposing (please reply w/ objections by EOD)
- Ship public launch when P0 are resolved + P1 have documented mitigations.
- Telemetry tags MUST be privacy-safe + opt-in. (Nikhil — please confirm this meets Hosted API requirements.)
- We prioritize: (a) default safety + supportability, (b) docs + doctor command for common misconfigs.

Owners / next steps (draft)
- Monica: engineering plan + scope cut recommendations for P0/P1
- Elliot: docs updates (troubleshooting page + “verify your traces” steps)
- Nikhil: confirm telemetry tagging constraints + what PM needs for KPI measurement if opt-in

Attachments:
- Internal Beta Feedback Rollup - 2025-03-10 (link)
- Launch Readiness Fix/Defer List v2 (PDF)

— Alex


From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Mar 10, 2025 at 10:03 AM
Subject: Re: Internal beta: feedback summary + decisions for public launch readiness (Quickstart Templates)

Agree with the prioritization. Quick engineering read:

P0 plan (what we can realistically land this week)
1) Telemetry header opt-in
- Template change: gate template tagging behind env var (e.g., REDWOOD_TEMPLATE_TELEMETRY=1)
- Default OFF in generated .env.example and README
- Also: make sure we’re not adding unknown headers by default in the HTTP client (TS + Python)
- I’ll also sanity-check gateway allowlist behavior from the platform PR that whitelists these headers

2) 429 defaults
- Lower default concurrency in the worker / request fanout path (both templates)
- Add jittered exponential backoff defaults; cap retries to avoid retry storms
- Update README to call out “Starter tier safe defaults” and a knob for power users

3) OTel exporter “no traces”
- Add more checks in CLI `doctor`:
  - confirm OTLP endpoint format
  - confirm collector reachable (health endpoint / TCP connect)
  - validate required env vars are set
- Provide a “local dev known good” docker-compose and point templates to it by default

4) Streaming disconnects
- Two parts:
  a) docs: recommended proxy settings + timeouts
  b) code: safer streaming retry that avoids duplicating the final answer on reconnect; at minimum: fail closed + actionable message when reconnect can’t be safely resumed
- I need Ibrahim/Dana to confirm what we can do in SDK vs template wrapper quickly. If SDK change is too risky, we’ll document hard guidance for launch and ship a follow-up SDK improvement.

P1 plan
- macOS install: add “preflight” section and known fix commands; pin any deps that are causing build failures
- Tool schema errors: improve error messages and log fields; add a “common causes” section + examples

Scope cut recommendation
- Defer any new vector store adapter work and any “upgrade in place” tooling. Keep it to init + doctor.

I’ll send a short tracker by end of day tying items to ENG-4186/4189/4184 plus the support tickets.

Monica
DevEx Engineering Lead
Redwood Inference


From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Mar 10, 2025 at 11:21 AM
Subject: Re: Internal beta: feedback summary + decisions for public launch readiness (Quickstart Templates)

+1. From docs side, we can reduce support load if we’re explicit about:

Docs changes I’ll land before launch
- Troubleshooting page updates with the “top 5” issues and copy-pastable fixes:
  - 401/403 (bad key / wrong env var)
  - 429 backoff + concurrency knobs
  - “no traces” and OTLP endpoint/auth checklist
  - streaming disconnect behind proxies (what to change in proxy + what to expect)
  - tool schema validation errors (example tool schema + what invalid output looks like)

- Add “Verify observability in 2 minutes” section in the template walkthrough:
  - run app
  - trigger request
  - see request_id in logs
  - see span in collector output (local)
  - see span in Console (hosted)

- Make the telemetry tagging section explicit: opt-in, what gets sent, what does NOT get sent, and how to disable.

I’ll also sync with Monica on naming consistency (env vars) so docs match the CLI doctor output.

Elliot
Docs Lead
Redwood Inference


From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Mar 10, 2025 at 12:07 PM
Subject: Re: Internal beta: feedback summary + decisions for public launch readiness (Quickstart Templates)

Telemetry constraints / PM requirements:

- Opt-in is acceptable and preferred given proxy behavior + privacy posture.
- The key is we still need a reliable way to measure:
  a) template activation (init -> first successful API call)
  b) template retention (repeat usage)
- We do NOT need any user content. No prompts, no retrieved chunks, no tool args.
- Allowed: a simple boolean template flag + template name/version + language (py/ts) + request_id correlation.

As long as the docs make it clear and the default is off, Hosted API PM is good with this plan.

Nikhil
PM, Hosted API
Redwood Inference


From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Mon, Mar 10, 2025 at 2:36 PM
Subject: Re: Internal beta: feedback summary + decisions for public launch readiness (Quickstart Templates)

Locking decisions for launch readiness:

Launch blockers (P0) — must be done before public launch
1) Telemetry tagging opt-in (default OFF) + docs language that it’s optional
2) Lower concurrency defaults + backoff guidance (avoid 429 “first impression”)
3) Doctor command catches “no traces” top misconfig paths (endpoint/auth/reachability)
4) Streaming behind proxies: either safer behavior or explicit docs + guardrails so we don’t create a support fire

Ship-with-mitigations (P1) — do if it’s clean, otherwise docs + known issues
- macOS python install friction: docs + pin deps; don’t block launch
- tool schema errors: improve messaging if possible; otherwise beef up troubleshooting examples

Defer (post-launch iteration)
- more vector store adapters
- more deployment recipes
- template upgrade-in-place tooling

Monica: please send the engineering tracker + dates once you’ve aligned w/ Ibrahim/Dana on streaming.
Elliot: please prioritize troubleshooting + “verify traces” steps.
Nikhil: thanks — please send any exact field names you want for the opt-in flag/version so we don’t churn.

— Alex

Tracker + ETA (high confidence unless SDK change balloons):

- Telemetry opt-in flag (templates + docs): Wed
- 429 defaults (concurrency + retries/backoff): Wed
- CLI doctor improvements for OTLP misconfig: Thu
- Streaming behind proxies:
  - docs guidance: Wed
  - code: aiming Fri; if SDK change is too risky, we’ll ship template-side fail-closed behavior + clear error + guidance and open an SDK follow-up

I’ll map these to existing tickets so we can track in one place:
- PM-912 (telemetry requirements)
- ENG-4184 (observability pack integration)
- ENG-4186 (streaming smoke tests)
- ENG-4189 (request id propagation)

Also: we’ll add a smoke test that reproduces the “unknown header blocked” behavior at least at a unit level (don’t send header by default).

Monica
